content: Calcium peroxide (CaO2) is a solid peroxide that appears as a white or yellowish substance. It is practically insoluble in water but dissolves in acidic solutions, producing hydrogen peroxide as a result. Upon contact with water, calcium peroxide rapidly decomposes, releasing oxygen. In agriculture, calcium peroxide is utilized as an oxygen-releasing fertilizer and is also employed in the pre-sowing treatment of rice seeds. In the aquaculture industry, it serves to oxygenate and disinfect water. Additionally, in the field of ecological restoration, calcium peroxide is used for soil treatment. It is applied in a manner similar to magnesium peroxide in environmental restoration programs, particularly for the remediation of soil and groundwater contaminated with petroleum hydrocarbons. This is achieved by enhancing aerobic microbial degradation of the contaminants through a process known as Enhanced In-Situ Bioremediation. As a food additive, calcium peroxide is assigned the E number E930. It is used as a flour bleaching agent and as an improving agent to enhance the quality of flour.
